Subject: Follow-up: POC scope and success criteria

Hi Marissa / Rishi -

Thanks for the call today - good overview of Redwood's serving options and the Dedicated trial path. Quick recap and asks to keep momentum: 

1) Goals/success criteria we discussed:
   - < 150ms 95th token latency on our 2k token average prompt mix
   - Average token cost <= $0.003 (target) for evaluation workload
   - No data egress from our VPC; logs retained for 30 days

2) Evaluation plan: 2-week POC against a 50k-query test set, split across our top 5 flows. We'll provide sample prompt set and expected label examples.

3) Timeline: hoping to start environment provisioning week of Jun 22 and run tests Jun 29-Jul 12.

Can you send the POC plan (owner, milestones, required inputs from our side) and a risk tracker we can use if we hit blockers? Also please confirm who we escalate to if we see infra-level 502s or timeouts.

Attaching our high-level requirements doc.

Best,
Paul
Director of Product
FinAnalyze

Hi Paul - thanks for the clear recap. Appreciate the targets - that helps us size the Dedicated pool and quantization profile.

Attached: POC-Plan-Finanalyze-v1.xlsx (owners, milestones, test dataset deadlines) and a starter POC-MAP. Highlights below:

- Success criteria (finalize during kickoff):
  * 95th token latency < 150ms on target prompt mix
  * Throughput to support 2.5 RPS sustained for the eval window
  * Quality: model output match rate >= 87% on your labelled sample
  * Security: no external egress; audit logs available for 30 days

- Evaluation plan (2 weeks):
  * Week 0 (provisioning): infra + model pin + data ingest (owner: Dev)
  * Week 1 (smoke + run 25k queries): baseline metrics + tweak batching
  * Week 2 (run remaining 25k + quality eval): collect samples for accuracy checks

- Owners: Marissa (customer success & coordination), Dev (infra/setup), Rishi (escalation & perf tuning), Lauren (contracts & billing)

- Next steps: confirm environment variables (VPC peering details + test dataset S3 link) by Wed Jun 24 so we can provision on Jun 25.

We'll also maintain a shared risk tracker (link in the workbook) to log blockers and mitigations - I'll add the initial rows.

Best,

Hi all - quick update from our initial smoke runs this morning:

- We hit intermittent 502 responses from the endpoint during the warmup step (see attached screenshot). Frequency ~ 5-8% during a 10-minute run.
- When successful, latency numbers are within expected range, but the instability prevents us from running the full 25k.

Questions:

2) We need an escalation contact for L2 if this persists since the POC schedule is tight.

Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC provisioning tasks + infra checklist

Hi Samantha - sorry for the disruption and thanks for flagging. We're treating this as a priority. Current status & mitigations: 

- Dev performed an initial node restart and found a bad kernel config causing occasional request drops. He pushed a fix and rebalanced the pool at 07:25 PT; early re-runs look good.
- Short-term mitigation: auto-restart policy tightened for the pool and increased health-check frequency.
- If you see >2% 502s in the next 2 hours, escalate to Rishi (rishi_malhotra@redwood.com). For unresolved production-impacting behavior beyond 60 minutes, our on-call L3 will engage (PagerDuty link in POC workbook).

I've opened SUP-1024 to track the bug and attached the Jira link in the tracker. Team will add root-cause analysis to the workbook after the 24-hour stability window.

Thanks for the patience - we'll confirm once the full 25k run completes without error.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Related: https://redwoodjira.internal/browse/SUP-1024
